text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Health Ministry imposing stringent checks and audits on doctors' records to maintain medical standards.
- Health Ministry to set limits on private hospital charges on patients using Medisave funds.

- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong's visit to China kicked off to good start with friendly tennis game with Li Ruihuan, chairman of China's top advisory body, Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference.
- Zurich cargo worker gets 50 Swiss francs from his boss as reward for spotting diamonds worth Singapore $15 million in a freight container.
- Some lucky primary schoolchildren get apportunities to attend grooming and social etiquette classes as part of their enrichment programmes.
- Port of Singapore Authority clinches 50-year contract to manage and develop Fuzhou Port.
- Creative Technology expecting 15 percent revenue growth and at least minimum of 30 percent gross margins for next fiscal year.
- Internet users to get speedier modems soon when 56kbps launched in Singapore commercially in next few weeks.
- Lum Chang Holdings chairman, Raymond Lum Kwan Sung denies insider trading allegations made against him by U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
- Jakarta property market in buoyant mood despite upcoming polls and fears of oversupply.
- Funds are fleeing most parts of Asia in favour of better performance in share markets elsewhere.
- Comfort Transportation and Tibs Taxis providing more Mercedes-Benzes to their fleets to provide premier service to customers.
- DBS Land confirms subsidiary Australand Holdings Pty Ltd, to go on public-listing in Australia and Singapore.
- The Stock Exchange of Singapore gives nod to Orchard Parade Holdings for two-for-five bonus issue.
